name: hightide
note: the whole flat LEDGE in front of the SEA CAVE -- from the dark cave mouth across to the foot of the stair and out to the rock lip over the sea -- is HIGH-TIDE ICE: clear, glassy sea ice like the frozen mere's blue ice but a little different -- greener-grey and wet-looking, with frozen-in bubbles and a few pale veins; scattered CLUMPS OF DARK KELP frozen into it and lying on it; a thin rime of white frost along its edges where it meets the rock; NO snow on it. The cave-mouth floor and the ledge are one continuous sheet of the same ice, joining seamlessly. The ICICLES hanging from the seaward lip stay exactly as painted; the cliffs, the stair, the three stone cairns and the open sea stay exactly as painted round it.
ruling: R-C9-339 the ledge as high-tide ice (Matt's idea)
